extracted.intended_audience: early-career independent investigators (assistant professors) and institutional officials managing limited-submission nominations for the Searle Scholars Program
extracted.subtask_description: Official program guidance describing who may be nominated and apply for Searle Scholars awards, the selection priorities, required institutional nomination procedures, deadlines, and how to appeal for institutional participation. Targets prospective applicants (assistant professors) and institutional limited-submission contacts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application submission route / nomination requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: "The Searle Scholars Program accepts applications only through an online application system." "Submissions are restricted to selected candidates from participating institutions only. Individuals who have not been nominated by a participating institution cannot apply."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Access to the online application will only be shared with nominated applicants. Individuals from participating institutions should consult their institution's limited submission contact for how the nomination process works. Nomination for the 2026 competition opens June 1, 2025; the application will be available to selected individuals once nomination has been placed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary selection focus: long-term innovative, high-impact potential
rubrics_metrics.description: "The Searle Scholars Scientific Advisory Board is primarily interested in the potential of applicants to make innovative and high-impact contributions to research over an extended period of time."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Selection emphasizes the applicant's potential for sustained innovation and significant scientific impact rather than short-term metrics. Applications should demonstrate promise for an extended independent research career.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligible research areas
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants are expected to be pursuing independent research careers in "biochemistry, cell biology, genetics, immunology, neuroscience, pharmacology, and related areas in chemistry, medicine, and the biological sciences."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should align their research scope with these fields. Those unsure whether their work fits are encouraged to examine research interests of present and former Searle Scholars listed on the program website.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required appointment timing and status
rubrics_metrics.description: "Applicants should have begun their appointment as an independent investigator at the assistant professor level on or after May 1, 2024. The appointment must be their first tenure-track position (or its nearest equivalent)."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Eligibility hinges on start date and that this is the applicant's first tenure-track (or nearest equivalent) independent appointment. Provide documentation or institutional confirmation as needed during nomination/application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institutions without tenure-track: prior consultation
rubrics_metrics.description: "Institutions which do not have tenure-track appointments should consult with the Scientific Director of the Program regarding eligibility of selected applicants PRIOR to nominating such individuals."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an institution's faculty titles/appointments differ from traditional tenure-track models, the institution must contact the Scientific Director before submitting a nomination to confirm eligibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clinical research limitation
rubrics_metrics.description: "The Searle Scholars Program does not ordinarily support purely clinical research but has supported research programs that include both clinical and basic components."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Purely clinical projects are generally ineligible; projects combining basic and clinical components may be acceptable. Applicants uncertain about fit should review past Scholars' research interests or contact the Scientific Director.

rubrics_metrics.name: Renomination of prior-year nominees
rubrics_metrics.description: "Applicants who were nominated for awards in the previous competition year but were not awarded may still meet the eligibility criteria for the current competition."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Institutions considering renomination of previously nominated-but-not-awarded individuals should consult with the Scientific Director regarding renomination procedures and eligibility continuity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection process and review body
rubrics_metrics.description: "Applications will be screened by a Scientific Advisory Board composed of experts in the fields of interest to the Program."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Peer experts on the Scientific Advisory Board conduct the screening/selection. Applicants should present clear evidence of scientific promise aligned with the Board's interests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification timeline
rubrics_metrics.description: All applicants "will be notified of competition results by the end of April of the award year."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan for decision communications by end of April; awards referenced in the page are activated July 1 of the award year (e.g., awards for the 2026 competition activate July 1, 2026).

rubrics_metrics.name: Competition schedule and deadlines
rubrics_metrics.description: For the 2026 competition: "Nomination for the 2026 competition will be open to participating institutions on June 1, 2025... the submission deadline will be September 30, 2025."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Key dates include nomination opening (June 1, 2025), application availability upon nomination, application submission deadline (September 30, 2025), award activation July 1, 2026, and finalist notification by end of April. Appeals to participate must arrive by February 1 for consideration in the next competition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeal process for institutional participation
rubrics_metrics.description: "Institutions that are not currently invited to participate... may send a one to two-page letter of appeal requesting inclusion in our competition. This letter should be signed by an appropriate institutional official... These requests are considered once a year, and must arrive in our office or be emailed... by February 1 for consideration in the next competition."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appeal letters should be 1–2 pages, signed by an appropriate official, addressed to the Scientific Advisory Board (mailing address provided) or emailed to searlescholars@kinshipfoundation.org. Include requested information (contact email, institutional overview emphasizing biomedical and chemistry departments, and any significant plans for faculty expansion, new facilities, or other research enhancements). The program will also review departmental websites when evaluating appeals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inquiries and points of contact
rubrics_metrics.description: "Questions about scientific aspects of an application or about eligibility should be addressed to the Scientific Director, other questions should be directed to Kinship Foundation staff."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Direct scientific/eligibility questions to the Scientific Director; administrative or process questions to Kinship Foundation staff (contact details provided on the page). Use institutional limited-submission contacts for internal nomination procedures.
